solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Our national drink

parts.note: the drink is crossword slang for the sea, and the sea round our own nation's coast has a special name

explanation.surface: A patriotic question about which beverage the nation calls its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like a beverage such as tea or beer, but in crosswords 'the drink' is the sea; ours is the stretch near our own shores.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal seas belonging to a country are its domestic territorial seas, so they are the nation's own sea, slangily its drink.

clue.text: Bowlers perhaps taken off to acclaim

definitions.text: Bowlers perhaps taken off to acclaim

parts.words: Bowlers perhaps taken off to acclaim
parts.note: bowlers are a style of headwear, which people remove in salute, as in the phrase for applauding someone

explanation.surface: Cricket bowlers being taken off after a fine spell to applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowlers' suggests cricketers; they are hard felt headgear, removed as a mark of admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowlers are an example of headgear, and doffing headwear is the traditional salute of admiration.

clue.text: Not having clue, misspelled 'diminutive'

parts.note: minus means without or not having

indicators.note: misspelled means the letters of the little word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A puzzled solver without a clue, spelling a word wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misspelled' rearranges CLUE to CULE. A sly joke: the answer is itself often misspelt with an I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minuscule is tiny, so it is a synonym for diminutive.

clue.text: Being withered, remove the inside and live

indicators.note: remove says some letters are to be taken out of the word withered
inside says the letters taken out come from the middle of that word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: cut out the dead heart of a withered plant and it will live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' looks like the verb to survive; it is the adjective for a cable carrying current, pronounced to rhyme with 'hive'.
explanation.definitionFit: A live circuit is connected to an electrical supply, so it is wired up and carrying current.

clue.text: Little Mary got cut, having tripped

parts.note: Little Mary is old British slang for the stomach, the tum
a cut person bled

explanation.surface: A small girl grazing herself after stumbling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' is a dated British nickname for the stomach, from a 1903 J. M. Barrie play.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tripped fell over, which is to have taken a tumble.

clue.text: Contacts and broaches subject of dismissing head

indicators.note: dismissing the head means the first letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: to bring up a matter is to broach a subject

explanation.surface: An executive phones staff and raises the topic of sacking the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a headteacher or boss; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To contact someone by phone is to telephone them, a British idiom for calling.

clue.text: Anglers play it on a line; others play a line on it

definitions.text: Anglers play it on a line
definitions.meaning: a fish anglers hook and tire out on a fishing line, a sea perch

definitions.text: others play a line on it
definitions.meaning: the low-pitched guitar or double ... on which musicians play the bottom line of a tune

explanation.surface: A neat contrast between fishermen and musicians, both playing lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sea fish caught by rod and the deep-voiced instrument carrying a band's lowest part.

clue.text: Adept in a new form of protection for the home front

indicators.note: in means the word for an expert goes inside the other two letters

parts.note: A as written plus N, the abbreviation for new
a pro is an adept or expert

explanation.surface: Wartime talk of a skilled new scheme for defending the home front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home front' sounds like wartime civil defence; here it is the front of a person doing housework.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore tied around the waist shields the front of one's clothes while cooking or cleaning at home.

clue.text: The star is twinkling outside little love

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters sit around the word for small
twinkling means the letters of the star are flickering into a new order

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A romantic night scene: a star twinkling beyond a small loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is twinkling' rearranges THE STAR to STHEART; 'outside' puts it around WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is a term of endearment for a darling, as is the answer.

clue.text: Turning right round one gives voice

indicators.note: turning something about means the assembled letters are read back to front
round means the abbreviation for right is placed around the word for one

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer's pirouette described as somehow producing a singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like a description of the singer; it reverses the whole container, made with 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is the high adult male singing voice, so it is one example of a voice.

clue.text: Males, I agree, when drunk can be animals

parts.note: men are males

indicators.note: when drunk means the following words stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A comment that men who agree to everything after drinking behave like beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges I AGREE to AGERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild creatures kept for show, so the word stands for a group of beasts.

clue.text: Try refitting an old vessel

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: refitting a ship rebuilds it, so the letters of an old are reassembled

explanation.surface: A shipyard suggestion to refit a former boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refitting' rearranges AN OLD to NDOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a Venetian rowing boat, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Jockeys are given these handicaps

definitions.meaning: riders sit on the leather seats strapped to horses
a verb meaning burdens or encumbers someone, as in being lumbered with a debt

explanation.surface: Racing talk: jockeys being allotted weights to carry in a handicap race.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, 'handicaps' suggests weights; here it is the verb meaning burdens.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders are given leather seats for their mounts, and to burden someone with a problem is to lumber them with it.

clue.text: Saw backing group

indicators.note: backing means the word for the saw is written in reverse order

parts.note: a tenon is a type of fine-toothed saw (a tenon saw), used for joinery

explanation.surface: Someone saw a band supporting the main act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is the carpenter's tool, here TENON as in tenon saw, which 'backing' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a set of nine musicians, so it is a particular musical group.

clue.text: Spoke about Italy — drink flowed

indicators.note: about means the word for speaking goes around the other pieces

parts.note: orated means spoke formally
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A speaker talking about Italy while the wine flowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowed' is the definition in the sense of arose or sprang from a source.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that originated sprang or issued from a source, as a stream flows from its spring.

clue.text: Put out a shade about being rudely awakened

indicators.note: about means the colour word wraps around the word for ejecting

parts.note: red is a shade or colour
to oust is to put out or expel

explanation.surface: Someone shoved out of bed, embarrassed and coloured, after a rough awakening.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rousted is to be dragged out of bed or roughly stirred into action, a forceful waking.

clue.text: Buildings, these sites grey with age

definitions.meaning: the sides of the forehead, where hair often goes grey first

explanation.surface: Ancient religious buildings standing on sites weathered grey over centuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sites' reads as building plots; they are the spots on the head beside the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrines are buildings for worship, and the flat sides of the head go grey early in life.

clue.text: Intend to support and love, when taken to quarters

parts.note: a prop is a support
love is zero in tennis, written as O
S and E are two compass quarters, south and east

explanation.surface: A soldier planning to stand by and cherish someone once billeted in quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' gives compass points: S and E here.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose doing something is to plan or mean to do it, a synonym for intend.

clue.text: Theirs got tangled in one, climbing

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: tangled means the letters of theirs are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Climbers whose ropes got tangled together while ascending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got tangled' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal; the jumbled letters sit within the word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something climbing is going up or increasing, as a rising price is.

clue.text: What Eddystone did in gale, damaged by sea

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the stormy word are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A lighthouse keeps shining through a storm battering the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddystone is a famous lighthouse off Plymouth in south-west England. 'damaged' rearranges GALE to GLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighthouse such as Eddystone shone out with bright flashes, so it glowed or glinted in the dark.

clue.text: Upset, I notice misinformation in part of the media

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
lies are misinformation

explanation.surface: An annoyed reader spotting falsehoods in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses I AD to DAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Dailies are newspapers published every day, a branch of the press.

clue.text: Poppycock! Vehicle should be taken back — get another!

definitions.note: another vehicle, the one the reversal produces

indicators.note: taken back means the words for nonsense and vehicle, together, are read from the end

parts.note: rot is nonsense or poppycock
a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An indignant customer returning a dud car and demanding a replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be taken back' reverses ROTCART. The definition is 'another', meaning another vehicle, of a different kind from the cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a farm vehicle, so it is another vehicle besides the cart in the wordplay.

clue.text: Start by giving time to manipulating fraud

parts.note: a rigger is someone who rigs, a fraud manipulating results

explanation.surface: A con artist beginning by setting a deadline for a rigged scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off or initiate it, so it means start as a verb.

clue.text: Half a month required by lecturer's book

indicators.note: half means only the first four of the eight letters of the month are kept

parts.note: November is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A lecturer assigning a book that must be read within a fortnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The month is NOVEMBER; its first half gives NOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a book-length piece of prose fiction, so it is a kind of book.

clue.text: To have and to hold, to love and to conjugate?

definitions.text: To have and to hold, to love and to conjugate?

parts.words: To have and to hold, to love and to conjugate?
parts.note: the wedding vow lists action words, and the comic addition shows they are words that are inflected for tense and person

explanation.surface: A grammarian's twist on the marriage vow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like the wedding service; the question mark warns that the infinitives are grammar examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Have, hold, love and conjugate are all doing-words that can be conjugated, so they are examples of this part of speech.

clue.text: Give impression of being single. Having wife, conceal it

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, means single

indicators.note: conceal means the word for a spouse hides the little word inside it

parts.note: a mate is a wife or partner
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a married person on pretending to be single while hiding a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' is the Roman numeral one; 'Having wife, conceal it' has the spouse word hide the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate someone is to mimic or impersonate them, which is doing an impression of them.

clue.text: Almost exhausted, found beside a tree

indicators.note: beside means the shortened word sits next to the single letter
almost means the word for worn out is used without its final letter

parts.note: spent means exhausted

explanation.surface: A weary walker collapsing next to a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar with trembling leaves, so it is one example of a tree.

clue.text: Not eaten, went off

explanation.surface: Food that was untouched because it had spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went off' suggests food turning bad; it means departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Untouched food is what remains on the plate, and someone who departed has gone away.

clue.text: Ill-considered article about corporal punishment

indicators.note: about means the word for an object goes around the word for hasty

parts.note: an article is an object or thing
rash means ill-considered or hasty

explanation.surface: A hasty newspaper piece on caning in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece or a grammatical 'the'; it is an object, THING.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrashing is a severe beating, a form of physical punishment.

clue.text: Best time of one's life is brief

definitions.meaning: the peak or heyday of a person's life
a verb meaning to prepare someone with information beforehand

explanation.surface: A wistful remark that one's golden years pass quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' reads as an adjective meaning short; it is the verb meaning to inform in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: One's heyday is the peak of life, and to fill someone in ahead of time is to prepare them.

clue.text: Record that's number one's by Cher — 'Missing Her'

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a number
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I and S

indicators.note: missing means the pronoun is dropped from the singer's name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chart-topping single by the singer Cher, titled 'Missing Her'.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals. 'Missing' removes HER from CHER, leaving C.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, so the word stands for a recording.

clue.text: Strain to reform man that's harsh

indicators.note: to reform is to remake, so the letters of strain are formed into a new order

parts.note: a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A tough regime that pushes a man to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges STRAIN to ASTRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent criticism is sharp and severe, so it means harsh or caustic.
